question: Should OpenClaw accept `agents.defaults.heartbeat.fallbacks` and `agents.list[].heartbeat.fallbacks` as the public heartbeat fallback policy surface, with omitted meaning normal fallback behavior and `[]` meaning strict fail-fast?
rationale: The implementation is narrow and appears coherent, but root policy treats new config/default and fallback surfaces as compatibility-sensitive public contracts that require maintainer API intent.

options.title: Accept sibling fallback keys
options.body: Proceed with this API shape once exact-head CI is green because it preserves default behavior and gives operators an explicit strict heartbeat policy.

options.title: Prefer object-form model config
options.body: Pause this PR and request a redesign if maintainers want heartbeat fallback policy to live under a `{ primary, fallbacks }` model object instead.

options.title: Defer heartbeat fallback policy
options.body: Keep heartbeat fallback behavior unchanged for now if maintainers do not want another heartbeat config key in this release train.

recommendation.title: Accept sibling fallback keys
recommendation.body: Proceed with this API shape once exact-head CI is green because it preserves default behavior and gives operators an explicit strict heartbeat policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main and earlier per-agent heartbeat config history make this the best available routing owner for the public config contract decision.
